gap: No result ChatGPT got states that MobileReviews Eh! bend-tested two USB4 240W cables to failure: the Cable Matters USB4 (0.6 m) failed every charging and data test after its ~10,000-bend test, and the Amazon Basics USB4 (1 m) went to 1 charge in 20 tries with data failed. The Mophie Charge Stream USB4 (0.8 m, $29.95) came through 11,000 bends with no meaningful change in voltage drop, resistance or speed.
standout_why: I opened ChatGPT's cited Plugable USB4-240W-1M page. It lists 240W and 40Gbps as separate ratings, never says they work at the same time, and has no measured throughput, voltage drop or durability figure. The other results (StarTech, ACT, Club 3D, Epico and Mouser datasheets, plus Staples, CDW, B&H and Best Buy listings) are spec or retail pages with no third-party measurements. ChatGPT's answer recommends a Cable Matters USB4 cable with no test data, and our current page lists Amazon Basics USB4 at $14.39 with no test data either.
decides: This confirms Plugable as the safer pick and argues against two cheap rows. The only named durability test of Cable Matters USB4 (ChatGPT's 'longer cable' pick) and Amazon Basics USB4 (on our page) shows both failing after about 10,000 bends. Mophie Charge Stream USB4 is the 240W USB4 cable with a named pass. Caveats: the Cable Matters cable tested was the 0.6 m version, not the 2 m one ChatGPT showed. MobileReviews Eh!'s drive capped every run at about 238 MB/s, so those tests don't verify 40Gbps, and their charging tests were not logged as 48 V/5 A figures. No named reviewer I could open has measured 240W and 40Gbps running at the same time on any candidate.
